contentBlocks.title: SASSA Limpopo Province
contentBlocks.description: Provincial hub for Limpopo beneficiaries: regional office contacts, how the vast rural mobile network operates, why bank transfer is recommended here, and local FAQs.

contentBlocks.collectionInfo: Limpopo's large rural network means many beneficiaries rely on mobile pay points and community hall collection days. Retail collection works well in towns; for remote villages, SASSA mobile units serve communities across Vhembe, Capricorn, Mopani and Sekhukhune districts.

contentBlocks.text: Full-service offices in Polokwane, Thohoyandou, Giyani, Mokopane and other district centres handle applications, reviews, card replacements and appeals support. The province spans a huge geographic area, so satellite points and scheduled mobile units bring services to villages that are far from any town — schedules are published monthly through tribal authority offices.

In towns like Polokwane, Tzaneen and Mokopane, SASSA card withdrawals at major retailers work exactly as elsewhere in the country. The provincial difference is distance: many beneficiaries travel significant distances to reach a retailer or pay point, which is why direct bank transfer is strongly recommended wherever a beneficiary has access to a bank account — money arrives without travel at all.

For villages without retail access, monthly mobile pay point visits are the primary channel. Plan around the published schedule: arrive early, bring your card and ID, and remember that uncollected money stays available — you will not lose a payment because you missed one visit day.

items: Switch to bank transfer to eliminate long trips to retailers.
Check mobile unit schedules at your local tribal authority office each month.
Thohoyandou serves the Vhembe district including Dzanani and Malamulele areas.
Staff can assist in Sepedi, Tshivenda and Xitsonga at all branches.

contentBlocks.title: Village scam warning
contentBlocks.text: Travelling 'agents' charging fees to 'register' beneficiaries for grants or collect money on their behalf operate in rural Limpopo. All legitimate SASSA services are free — never hand over your card or PIN to anyone.

faqs.question: How do I find rural pay points in Limpopo?
faqs.answer: SASSA publishes monthly schedules of community halls and mobile trucks serving remote areas. Local tribal authority offices also display current visit dates.

faqs.question: Which office serves the Vhembe district?
faqs.answer: The Thohoyandou SASSA office serves Vhembe, with mobile pay points covering outlying villages such as Dzanani and Malamulele.

faqs.question: Can I get help in my home language?
faqs.answer: Yes — Sepedi, Tshivenda, Xitsonga and other local languages are supported at Limpopo branches.

faqs.question: Are there enough retail pay points in rural areas?
faqs.answer: Retailers concentrate in towns. Deep rural beneficiaries should use bank transfer or scheduled mobile pay points, and plan collection trips in advance.

faqs.question: What if I miss the mobile pay point day in my village?
faqs.answer: Your money is not lost — balances carry over until you collect. Check when the unit next visits, or switch to bank transfer to avoid future dependence on the schedule.
